passages.title: 收據背面的祕密
passages.text: Every Saturday, Mom sends me to the {1} near our apartment to buy milk and eggs. Last week, when I paid, the cashier gave me my {2} with a big smile. On the way home, I turned it over. On the back, someone had written in small letters: "Have a nice day! You are doing great." I was {3}. It was a hard week at school, and those words made me feel much better. The next Saturday, I went back and paid in {4} again. This time I gave the cashier a note too: "Thank you. Your message made my day." She read it and laughed. Now we write short notes to each other every week. Mom says I am the only kid who {5} buying eggs so much.

blanks.why: the supermarket「超市」：去買牛奶和蛋。fever（發燒）、throat（喉嚨）、knee（膝蓋）都不是可以買東西的地方。
receipt「收據」：結帳時收銀員給我收據，後面說翻到背面有字。cough、toe、lemon 都不是結帳時拿到的紙。
be surprised「感到驚訝」：看到背面的鼓勵字句很意外。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能形容心情。
pay in cash「付現金」是固定說法。fever、knee、spoon 都不能放在 pay in 後面表示付款方式。
enjoy + V-ing「喜歡做某事」：我是唯一這麼喜歡買蛋的小孩。fries、boils、spells 都不能接 buying eggs。

passages.zh: 每個星期六，媽媽都會叫我去我們公寓附近的超市買牛奶和蛋。上星期我付錢時，收銀員笑著把收據遞給我。回家路上，我把收據翻過來，發現背面有人用小小的字寫著：「祝你有美好的一天！你做得很好。」我很驚訝。那一週在學校過得很辛苦，這幾個字讓我心情好多了。下個星期六，我又去了，一樣付現金，這次我也給了收銀員一張紙條：「謝謝你，你的話讓我開心了一整天。」她看了之後笑了出來。現在我們每個星期都會互寫小紙條。媽媽說，我是唯一一個這麼喜歡去買蛋的小孩。

passages.title: 阿嬤的折價券資料夾
passages.text: My grandma has a thick blue folder. Inside, there are hundreds of {1} from newspapers and flyers. She sorts them by date and by store. Every morning, she checks which ones are still good. Last Sunday, she took me to a big {2} store. She used one coupon for towels, one for a frying pan, and one for my new school bag. The cashier added everything up and said, "You saved 1,500 dollars!" The people in line behind us {3} for her. Grandma looked very proud. On the way home, she gave me a small folder of my own. "Start {4} now," she said. "When you have a family, you will thank me." I keep my folder next to my bed, and I even check the {5} flyers every week now.

blanks.why: coupons「折價券」：從報紙和傳單剪下來，依日期整理。coughs、knees、fevers 都不能放在資料夾裡。
department store「百貨公司」是固定說法。throat、spoon、toe 不能和 store 組成這個地方。
cheer for + 人「為某人歡呼」：排在後面的人為她歡呼。fried、boiled、spelled 都不能接 for her 表示讚美。
start + V-ing「開始做…」：現在就開始收集。frying、boiling、spelling 都和折價券資料夾無關。
supermarket flyers「超市的傳單」。fever、lemon、knee 都不會印傳單。

passages.zh: 我阿嬤有一個厚厚的藍色資料夾，裡面有幾百張從報紙和傳單上剪下來的折價券。她把它們按照日期和店家分類，每天早上都會檢查哪些還能用。上個星期天，她帶我去一家大百貨公司。她用了一張折價券買毛巾、一張買平底鍋，還有一張買我的新書包。收銀員算好之後說：「您省了一千五百元！」排在我們後面的人都為她歡呼，阿嬤看起來很驕傲。回家路上，她給了我一個屬於我自己的小資料夾。「現在就開始收集吧，」她說，「等你有了家庭，你會感謝我的。」我把資料夾放在床邊，現在每個星期還會看超市的傳單。

passages.title: 試吃大軍
passages.text: My little brother Tim loves free samples. Every time we go to the {1}, he walks slowly past every table. He tries sausages, cheese, dumplings, and juice. One Sunday, Mom said, "Tim, we are here to buy food, not to eat it all for free!" But Tim had a plan. He took a {2} from the sausage table and gave it to Mom. "Look! If you buy two bags, you get one free," he said. Mom {3} the price. It was a good deal, so she bought them. At the counter, she paid in {4} and looked at the long {5}. "Okay," she laughed, "your free lunch finally saved us some money." Tim was very proud of himself and said he would find more coupons next week.

blanks.why: the supermarket「超市」，有試吃攤位。cough、throat、toe 都不是地點。
coupon「折價券」：從香腸攤拿的，買兩包送一包。fever、knee、spoon 都不會寫優惠內容。
checked the price「看了一下價格」。fried、boiled、spelled 接 the price 都不通。
pay in cash「付現金」。throat、sock、lemon 都不能放在 pay in 後面表示付款方式。
the long receipt「長長的收據」：買東西後看收據。knee、cough、fever 都不會是「長長的」結帳紙。

passages.zh: 我弟弟 Tim 超愛免費試吃。每次我們去超市，他都會慢慢地經過每一個試吃攤，香腸、起司、水餃、果汁都要吃一口。有個星期天，媽媽說：「Tim，我們是來買東西的，不是來把東西全部免費吃光的！」但 Tim 早有計畫。他從香腸攤拿了一張折價券給媽媽。「你看！買兩包送一包。」他說。媽媽看了看價格，覺得很划算，就買了。到了櫃台，她付了現金，看著長長的收據笑著說：「好啦，你的免費午餐總算幫我們省了一點錢。」Tim 對自己非常得意，還說下星期要找更多折價券。

passages.title: 洗衣機裡的鈔票
passages.text: On Monday morning, Dad couldn't find his wallet. He {1} everywhere: in the car, under the sofa, and even in the fridge. Then Mom opened the washing machine and screamed. Dad's wallet was inside, and so was all his {2}! The bills were wet and stuck together. There was also a long {3} from the supermarket. It was now just a ball of soft white paper. Dad sat down and laughed. "Well, at least my money is clean now," he joked. We put the bills on the table to dry. Luckily, most of them were fine. Dad used them to buy breakfast the next day, but he had to {4} to the clerk why they looked so strange. Now Mom always checks every {5} before she washes clothes.

blanks.why: look everywhere「到處找」。fried、boiled、spelled 接 everywhere 都不通。
all his cash「他所有的現金」：後面說鈔票濕了黏在一起。knee、cough、throat 都不會放在錢包裡。
a long receipt「一張長長的收據」，洗過後變成一團軟紙。fever、toe、spoon 都不會變成紙團。
explain to + 人「向某人解釋」：他得跟店員解釋鈔票為什麼長這樣。fry、boil、spell 都不能接 to the clerk why…。
check every pocket「檢查每個口袋」才不會把東西洗進去。lemon（檸檬）、bean（豆子）、cough（咳嗽）都不是衣服上裝東西的地方。

passages.zh: 星期一早上，爸爸找不到他的錢包。他到處找：車上、沙發底下，連冰箱都找過了。後來媽媽打開洗衣機，尖叫了一聲——爸爸的錢包就在裡面，他所有的現金也是！鈔票濕答答地黏在一起，還有一張超市的長收據，現在已經變成一團軟軟的白紙。爸爸坐下來哈哈大笑。「至少我的錢現在很乾淨了。」他開玩笑說。我們把鈔票攤在桌上晾乾，還好大部分都沒事。隔天爸爸用那些錢買早餐，但他得跟店員解釋為什麼鈔票看起來這麼奇怪。現在媽媽洗衣服前都會檢查每一個口袋。

passages.title: 頂樓的舊遊樂場
passages.text: When my dad was a child, the old {1} store in our city had a small amusement park on the roof. There was a merry-go-round, a tiny train, and a machine that gave out candy. Every Sunday, Grandpa took him there. The rides did not take {2}. Instead, you bought paper tickets at the entrance. Dad still has one old ticket and a faded {3} from 1988 in his drawer. Last year, the store closed, and the roof park was {4} down. Dad was sad, so he took me to the roof before it was gone. We stood there quietly and looked at the city. "This was my {5} place in the whole world," he said softly. Then he took out the old ticket and gave it to me. "Now it is your treasure," he said.

blanks.why: department store「百貨公司」。knee、throat、cough 不能和 store 組成地點。
take cash「收現金」：遊樂設施不收現金，要買紙票。fever、toe、spoon 都不是錢。
a faded receipt「一張褪色的收據」，和舊票一起收在抽屜。lemon、sock、bean 放三十多年不會說是「1988 年的…」紀念品。
be taken down「被拆除」：take down 是「拆掉」。fried、boiled、spelled 都不能和 down 組成「拆除」的意思。
my favorite place「我最喜歡的地方」。salty、sour、thirsty 都不能用來形容一個地方。

passages.zh: 我爸爸小時候，我們城市那家老百貨公司的頂樓有一座小小的遊樂園，有旋轉木馬、迷你火車，還有一台會掉出糖果的機器。每個星期天，阿公都會帶他去。遊樂設施不收現金，要在入口買紙票。爸爸的抽屜裡到現在還留著一張舊票，和一張 1988 年、已經褪色的收據。去年那家百貨公司結束營業，頂樓的遊樂園也被拆了。爸爸很難過，就在拆掉之前帶我上了頂樓。我們靜靜地站在那裡看著城市。「這裡曾經是我在全世界最喜歡的地方。」他輕聲說。接著他拿出那張舊票交給我。「現在它是你的寶貝了。」他說。

passages.title: 超市裡走失的狗
passages.text: On a rainy afternoon, a wet little dog ran into our neighborhood {1}. It went straight to the meat section and sat down. The workers tried to {2} it, but it was too fast. Customers laughed as it ran between the shelves. Finally, a girl gave it a piece of bread, and it stopped running. There was a phone number on its collar, so the manager called the owner. Twenty minutes later, an old man came in. "Lucky! There you are!" he shouted. To say thank you, he bought a big bag of dog food and a cake for the workers. He paid in {3} and left a {4} for free coffee for the girl. The store kept his {5} on the wall, with a photo of Lucky.

blanks.why: supermarket「超市」，有肉品區和貨架。fever、throat、toe 都不是地點。
try to catch it「試著抓住牠」，後面說牠太快了。fry、boil、spell 接 it（狗）都不合理。
pay in cash「付現金」。knee、lemon、cough 不能放在 pay in 後面。
a coupon for free coffee「免費咖啡兌換券」。sock、spoon、bean 都不能接 for free coffee 表示可以兌換。
kept his receipt on the wall「把他的收據貼在牆上」當紀念。toe、fever、throat 都不能貼在牆上。

passages.zh: 一個下雨的午後，一隻濕答答的小狗跑進我們社區的超市。牠直接衝到肉品區坐了下來。員工們想抓住牠，但牠跑得太快了，客人們看著牠在貨架間跑來跑去都笑了。最後，一個女孩給了牠一塊麵包，牠才停下來。牠的項圈上有一支電話號碼，店長就打電話給主人。二十分鐘後，一位老先生走了進來。「Lucky！原來你在這裡！」他大喊。為了道謝，他買了一大袋狗飼料和一個蛋糕送給員工。他付了現金，還留了一張免費咖啡兌換券給那個女孩。超市把他的收據貼在牆上，旁邊還有一張 Lucky 的照片。

passages.title: 中了一千元的發票
passages.text: In Taiwan, every {1} from a store is also a lottery ticket. Every two months, the government {2} the winning numbers. Most people just throw their receipts away, but my aunt keeps all of them in a big box. Last month, she asked me to help her check them. We spent two hours reading numbers. Suddenly, I shouted, "Auntie, this one won 1,000 dollars!" It was from a small {3} where she bought a bottle of soy sauce. We were so happy. She went to the post office and got the money in {4}. Then she took me to the {5} store and bought me a new pair of sneakers. "You found it, so you deserve a gift," she said.

blanks.why: every receipt「每一張收據（發票）」都是彩券。fever、cough、knee 都不能拿來對獎。
choose the winning numbers「選出中獎號碼」。fries、boils、spells 接號碼都不通。
a small supermarket「一家小超市」，她在那裡買了醬油。throat、toe、lemon 都不是商店。
get the money in cash「領到現金」。spoon、sock、bean 都不能放在 in 後面表示錢的形式。
department store「百貨公司」，去那裡買球鞋。knee、fever、cough 不能和 store 組成地點。

passages.zh: 在台灣，每一張商店的收據（發票）也是一張彩券，政府每兩個月會選出中獎號碼。大部分的人都直接把發票丟掉，但我阿姨會把它們全部收在一個大盒子裡。上個月，她請我幫她對發票，我們花了兩個小時看號碼。突然我大叫：「阿姨，這張中了一千元！」那是她在一家小超市買一瓶醬油的發票。我們好開心。她去郵局領了現金，然後帶我去百貨公司，買了一雙新球鞋給我。「是你找到的，你值得一份禮物。」她說。

passages.title: 殭屍也要逛超市
passages.text: In the town of Grayhill, zombies are not scary. They are just a little slow. Every Thursday night, the {1} opens late just for them. The zombies push their carts very, very slowly. They love {2} for brain-shaped jelly and cold soup. The clerks are patient. "Take your time, Mr. Bones," they say with a smile. Zombies never use cards. They always pay in {3}, and the coins are often a hundred years old! Last week, a zombie named Ruby brought a {4} for 50% off. "I found it in my grave," she said. The clerk checked it and laughed. It was from 1923. She still gave Ruby the discount and a free {5} holder as a gift. Ruby was so happy that she smiled, and one of her teeth fell out.

blanks.why: the supermarket「超市」為殭屍晚開。cough、knee、fever 都不是商店。
look for「尋找」：他們喜歡找大腦形狀的果凍。frying、boiling、spelling 都不能和 for 搭配表示「找」。
pay in cash「付現金」，後面說硬幣有一百年歷史。throat、toe、spoon 不能放在 pay in 後面。
a coupon for 50% off「半價折價券」。lemon、bean、sock 都不能表示打折。
a receipt holder「收據夾」。fever、knee、throat 都不能接 holder 當成禮物。

passages.zh: 在灰丘鎮，殭屍一點也不可怕，只是動作有點慢。每個星期四晚上，超市都會為了他們晚點打烊。殭屍們推著推車，非常非常慢地前進。他們最喜歡找大腦形狀的果凍和冷湯。店員們都很有耐心。「慢慢來，骨頭先生。」他們笑著說。殭屍從來不用卡，總是付現金，而且硬幣常常已經有一百年歷史了！上星期，一個叫 Ruby 的殭屍帶來一張半價折價券。「我在我的墳墓裡找到的。」她說。店員一看就笑了，那是 1923 年的。她還是給了 Ruby 折扣，還送她一個收據夾當禮物。Ruby 開心得笑了出來，結果掉了一顆牙。

passages.title: 百貨公司的玩具部
passages.text: When I was six, my favorite place was the toy {1} on the fifth floor of a big store downtown. There were trains, robots, dolls, and a huge box of colorful balls. I could stay there for hours. One day, I wanted a red fire truck, but Mom said it was too {2}. I cried and refused to leave. A kind clerk came over and showed me a small {3} book. "If your mom buys something today, she can get 30% off next time," she said. Mom smiled and bought me a small puzzle. Two weeks later, we came back, and the fire truck was cheaper with the coupon. Mom paid in {4}. I still have the fire truck, and Mom still has the {5} in her old photo album.

blanks.why: the toy department「玩具部（玩具區）」：百貨公司的部門。throat、fever、cough 都不能和 toy 組成一個賣場區域。
too expensive「太貴」，後面用折價券才變便宜。lazy、rude、thirsty 都不能形容玩具價錢。
a coupon book「折價券本」：下次可以打七折。knee、toe、lemon 都不能和 book 組成這個意思。
pay in cash「付現金」。fever、bean、sock 不能放在 pay in 後面。
the receipt「收據」被收在相簿裡當紀念。spoon、cough、throat 都不會被收進相簿當作購買紀錄。

passages.zh: 我六歲的時候，最喜歡的地方是市中心一家大百貨公司五樓的玩具部。那裡有火車、機器人、娃娃，還有一大箱彩色的球，我可以在那裡待好幾個小時。有一天，我想要一台紅色消防車，但媽媽說太貴了。我哭著不肯走。一位親切的店員走過來，給我看一本小小的折價券本。「如果媽媽今天買個東西，下次就可以打七折喔。」她說。媽媽笑了笑，買了一盒小拼圖給我。兩個星期後我們又回去了，用折價券買消防車便宜多了。媽媽付了現金。那台消防車我到現在都還留著，媽媽也還把那張收據收在她的舊相簿裡。

passages.title: 過期一天的折價券
passages.text: Mia had a coupon for a free ice cream at the {1} near her school. She wanted to use it on a hot day. On Friday, the sun was strong, so she finally went. But at the counter, the cashier looked at the {2} and shook her head. "I'm sorry. It ended yesterday." Mia was so {3} that she almost cried. She didn't have any {4} with her, so she couldn't buy one either. An old man behind her heard everything. He bought two ice creams and gave one to Mia. "A hot day needs ice cream," he said. Mia thanked him again and again. Then she {5} an important lesson: always check the date on a coupon, and always be kind to strangers.

blanks.why: the supermarket「超市」。knee、fever、cough 都不是地方。
looked at the coupon「看了折價券」，說它昨天就到期了。throat、toe、bean 都不會到期。
so disappointed that…「失望到…」。salty、sour、spicy 是味道，不能形容心情。
have cash with her「身上帶著現金」：沒帶錢，所以也買不了。spoon、lemon、sock 和買冰淇淋付錢無關。
learned a lesson「學到教訓」。fried、boiled、spelled 接 a lesson 都不通。

passages.zh: Mia 有一張可以在學校附近超市兌換免費冰淇淋的折價券，她想在大熱天用。星期五太陽很大，她終於去了。可是到了櫃台，收銀員看了看折價券，搖搖頭說：「不好意思，它昨天就到期了。」Mia 失望得差點哭出來。她身上沒帶現金，也沒辦法自己買。排在她後面的一位老先生聽到了一切，他買了兩支冰淇淋，把其中一支送給 Mia。「大熱天就是需要冰淇淋。」他說。Mia 一直向他道謝。她學到了重要的一課：一定要看清楚折價券上的日期，也要對陌生人友善。

passages.title: 只收現金的牛肉麵攤
passages.text: Near the train station in Tainan, there is a beef noodle stand that has been open for forty years. The owner, Mr. Kuo, only takes {1}. There is a big sign that says "No cards, no phones, no {2}." Some young tourists get angry when they see it, but most people don't mind. The soup is that good. Last summer, a family from Japan came to eat there. They didn't have any Taiwan dollars, so Mr. Kuo pointed to the {3} across the street. "There is a cash machine inside," he said. The family came back ten minutes later. After eating, the father asked for a {4} to keep as a memory. Mr. Kuo laughed and wrote one by hand. "Come back again," he said. "The soup will {5} for you."

blanks.why: only takes cash「只收現金」。fever、knee、cough 都不能當付款方式。
no coupons「不收折價券」，和 cards、phones 一樣是付款或優惠方式。throats、toes、lemons 都不會寫在付款規定上。
the supermarket across the street「對街的超市」，裡面有提款機。sock、spoon、bean 都不是建築物。
ask for a receipt「要一張收據」當紀念，後面老闆手寫一張。knee、cough、fever 都不能用手寫。
wait for you「等你」：湯會等你回來。fry、boil、spell 都不能接 for you 表示等待。

passages.zh: 台南火車站附近有一家開了四十年的牛肉麵攤，老闆郭先生只收現金。攤子上有一塊大招牌寫著：「不收卡、不收手機付款、不收折價券。」有些年輕觀光客看到會生氣，但大部分的人都不介意，因為湯實在太好喝了。去年夏天，一個從日本來的家庭來吃麵。他們身上沒有台幣，郭先生就指了指對街的超市：「裡面有提款機。」十分鐘後，這家人回來了。吃完之後，爸爸要了一張收據當紀念。郭先生笑著手寫了一張。「再來喔，」他說，「這碗湯會等你們。」

passages.title: 被弟弟改過的購物清單
passages.text: Mom wrote a shopping list and asked my brother Ken and me to go to the {1}. She gave us 500 dollars in {2} and said, "Buy only what is on the list." On the way, Ken took the list and secretly added "chocolate," "chips," and "cola" at the bottom. I didn't notice. At the store, we bought everything. When we got home, Mom looked at the {3} and frowned. "I didn't write chocolate," she said. Ken tried to look innocent, but his face turned red. Mom didn't get angry. Instead, she {4} and said, "Next time, use your own money." Then she cut out a {5} for chocolate from the newspaper and gave it to him. "But this will help," she said with a wink.

blanks.why: go to the supermarket「去超市」買清單上的東西。throat、toe、cough 都不是地點。
500 dollars in cash「五百元現金」。knee、fever、spoon 都不能接在 in 後面表示錢的形式。
looked at the receipt「看收據」，發現買了巧克力。lemon、bean、sock 上面不會列出買了什麼。
laughed「笑了」，和前面 didn't get angry 呼應。fried、boiled、spelled 都不能表示她的反應。
a coupon for chocolate「巧克力折價券」，從報紙剪下來。cough、fever、throat 都不能從報紙剪下來。

passages.zh: 媽媽寫了一張購物清單，叫我和弟弟 Ken 去超市。她給了我們五百元現金，說：「只能買清單上的東西。」路上，Ken 拿走清單，偷偷在最下面加了「巧克力」、「洋芋片」和「可樂」，我都沒發現。到了店裡，我們把東西全買了。回家後，媽媽看著收據皺起眉頭。「我沒有寫巧克力啊。」她說。Ken 想裝無辜，但臉都紅了。媽媽沒有生氣，反而笑著說：「下次用你自己的錢。」接著她從報紙上剪下一張巧克力折價券給他。「不過這個會有幫助的。」她眨眨眼說。

passages.title: 沒有收據的退貨
passages.text: Last weekend, I bought a pair of headphones at a {1} store. When I got home, I found that the left side didn't work. The next day, I went back to return them. "Do you have the {2}?" asked the clerk. I checked my bag and my pockets, but I couldn't find it. I think I threw it away with the shopping bag. The clerk was {3}, but she said she couldn't give my money back without it. I felt terrible. Then I remembered that I paid with Dad's credit card, not in {4}. The clerk checked her computer and found my order. "You're lucky," she said. She gave me a new pair. Since then, I always {5} my receipts in a small box for at least a month.

blanks.why: department store「百貨公司」。knee、fever、throat 不能和 store 組成地點。
the receipt「收據」：退貨要看收據。cough、toe、spoon 都不是退貨要出示的東西。
polite「有禮貌的」，but 後面是她不能退錢。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能形容人。
in cash「用現金」，和 with Dad's credit card 對比：刷卡才能在電腦查到紀錄。lemon、bean、sock 都不能當付款方式。
keep my receipts「保留收據」。fry、boil、spell 接 receipts 都不通。

passages.zh: 上週末，我在一家百貨公司買了一副耳機。回家後發現左邊沒有聲音。隔天，我回去要退貨。「請問有收據嗎？」店員問。我翻遍了包包和口袋都找不到，我想應該是跟購物袋一起丟掉了。店員很有禮貌，但她說沒有收據就不能退錢。我覺得糟透了。後來我想起來，我是用爸爸的信用卡付的，不是付現金。店員在電腦上查，找到了我的購買紀錄。「你很幸運。」她說，然後給了我一副新的。從那之後，我都會把收據收在一個小盒子裡，至少放一個月。

passages.title: 爸爸的超市大冒險
passages.text: Dad never goes shopping. Mom usually does it. But last Saturday, Mom was sick in bed, so Dad had to go to the {1} alone. "How hard can it be?" he said. Two hours later, he was still not home. Mom called him. "I can't find the soy sauce!" he said. "And why are there twenty kinds of rice?" When he finally came back, he had three bags of snacks, a big watermelon, and no soy sauce. He also forgot to use Mom's {2}, so everything was full price. Mom looked at the long {3} and sighed. "You spent 2,000 dollars on snacks?" Dad smiled. "I was {4}," he said. Mom laughed so hard that she started coughing. The next week, Dad went shopping again. This time, he {5} a list.

blanks.why: go to the supermarket「去超市」。fever、cough、toe 都不是地點。
Mom's coupons「媽媽的折價券」：沒用到，所以都是原價。knees、throats、lemons 和「原價」無關。
the long receipt「長長的收據」，看了才知道花了兩千元買零食。spoon、bean、sock 上面不會有金額。
I was hungry.「我餓了。」解釋為什麼買那麼多零食。salty、sour、spicy 是食物的味道，不能形容人的狀態。
brought a list「帶了清單」。fried、boiled、spelled 接 a list 都不通。

passages.zh: 爸爸從來不去買菜，平常都是媽媽去。但上星期六媽媽生病躺在床上，爸爸只好一個人去超市。「能有多難？」他說。兩個小時後，他還沒回家。媽媽打電話給他。「我找不到醬油！」他說，「而且為什麼米有二十種？」等他終於回來，手上有三袋零食、一顆大西瓜，卻沒有醬油。他也忘了用媽媽的折價券，所以全部都是原價。媽媽看著長長的收據嘆了一口氣：「你花了兩千元買零食？」爸爸笑著說：「我肚子餓嘛。」媽媽笑到咳個不停。下個星期，爸爸又去買菜了，這次他帶了一張清單。

passages.title: 惡龍的寶藏
passages.text: High on a mountain lived a dragon named Grumble. People said he had a cave full of gold. One day, a brave girl named Tess climbed up to find the treasure. When she entered the cave, she saw no gold at all. Instead, there were thousands of {1} from every store in the kingdom. "Gold is boring," Grumble said. "With these, I can get 50% off at any {2} in the land!" Tess laughed. "But dragons can't go shopping. Everyone is afraid of you." Grumble looked sad. So Tess made him an offer. She would {3} his food for him every week, and he would give her one coupon each time. Grumble agreed. He even gave her a bag of old {4} from his bed. Now Tess shops for a dragon, and she always brings him the {5} so he can check the prices.

blanks.why: thousands of coupons「好幾千張折價券」，後面說可以打五折。coughs、knees、fevers 都不能放在洞裡當寶藏。
any supermarket「任何一家超市」。throat、toe、lemon 都不是商店。
get his food「幫他買（取得）食物」，龍不能去買東西，所以 Tess 幫他買。spell（拼字）、sneeze（打噴嚏）、shout（大叫）接 his food 都不通。
a bag of old cash「一袋舊鈔票」。spoon、sock、bean 不能當成付給 Tess 的錢。
bring him the receipt「把收據帶給他」讓他檢查價格。fever、cough、throat 上面不會有價格。

passages.zh: 高高的山上住著一隻叫 Grumble 的龍，大家都說他有一個裝滿黃金的洞穴。有一天，一個名叫 Tess 的勇敢女孩爬上山去找寶藏。她走進洞裡，卻一塊黃金都沒看到，取而代之的是來自王國每家商店的好幾千張折價券。「黃金很無聊，」Grumble 說，「有了這些，我在這片土地上任何一家超市都能打五折！」Tess 笑了：「可是龍不能去買東西啊，大家都怕你。」Grumble 看起來很難過。於是 Tess 提出一個建議：她每個星期幫他買食物，他每次給她一張折價券。Grumble 答應了，甚至還從床底下拿出一袋舊鈔票給她。現在 Tess 幫一隻龍買菜，而且每次都會把收據帶給他，讓他檢查價格。

passages.title: 停電的超市
passages.text: Last Friday evening, the power went out in our whole neighborhood. I was at the {1} with my mom at the time. Suddenly, all the lights went off, and the cash registers stopped working. People couldn't pay with cards or phones. The manager stood on a chair and shouted, "We can only take {2} now!" Luckily, Mom had some money in her wallet. The cashiers used flashlights and calculators to add up the prices. They couldn't print a {3}, so they wrote everything by hand. It was slow, but nobody complained. Some people even {4} to hold flashlights for the workers. When we walked out, the stars were very bright. Mom said, "Sometimes a little trouble brings people {5}." Later, a cashier told us that when the lights came back, everyone in the store clapped.

blanks.why: at the supermarket「在超市」。knee、cough、throat 都不是地點。
take cash「收現金」：停電刷卡機不能用。toe、fever、spoon 都不能當付款方式。
print a receipt「印收據」：印不出來所以用手寫。lemon、bean、sock 都不是印表機印出來的東西。
offer to + 原形動詞「主動提議做…」：有人主動幫員工拿手電筒。fried、boiled、spelled 都不能接 to hold。
bring people together「讓大家團結在一起」。salty、sour、spicy 都不能放在 bring people 後面。

passages.zh: 上星期五傍晚，我們整個社區都停電了。當時我正和媽媽在超市裡。突然所有的燈都熄了，收銀機也停了，大家都不能用卡或手機付款。店長站到椅子上大喊：「現在只能收現金！」還好媽媽的錢包裡有一些錢。收銀員用手電筒和計算機來算價錢，因為印不出收據，所以全部用手寫。雖然很慢，但沒有人抱怨，有些人甚至主動幫員工拿手電筒照明。我們走出超市時，星星好亮。媽媽說：「有時候，一點小麻煩反而會讓大家團結在一起。」後來一位收銀員告訴我們，電來的那一刻，店裡的每個人都拍起手來。

passages.title: 公園長椅上的信封
passages.text: On my way home from school, I saw a brown envelope on a park bench. I opened it and found 20,000 dollars in {1}! There was also a {2} from a hospital inside. My heart beat fast. I could buy a new game, new shoes, and lots of snacks. But then I began to {3} about the person who lost it. Maybe the money was for someone who was sick. So I took the envelope to the police station. An hour later, an old woman came in, crying. The money was for her husband's medicine. She hugged me and gave me a {4} for a free dinner at her son's restaurant. That night, my parents said they were very {5} of me. That felt better than any new game.

blanks.why: 20,000 dollars in cash「兩萬元現金」。knee、cough、toe 都不能接在 in 後面表示錢的形式。
a receipt from a hospital「醫院的收據」，後面才會想到錢可能是給病人用的。fever 雖然和生病有關，但不能放在信封裡；spoon、throat 也不行。
worry about…「擔心…」：我開始擔心掉錢的人。fry、boil、spell 都不能接 about the person。
a coupon for a free dinner「一張免費晚餐券」。lemon、bean、sock 都不能兌換晚餐。
be proud of + 人「以某人為榮」。salty、sour、spicy 不能接 of me。

passages.zh: 放學回家的路上，我在公園的長椅上看到一個牛皮紙信封。我打開一看，裡面竟然有兩萬元現金！還有一張醫院的收據。我的心跳得好快：我可以買新遊戲、新鞋子，還有好多零食。但後來我開始擔心掉錢的人，也許這筆錢是要給生病的人用的。於是我把信封送到警察局。一個小時後，一位老奶奶哭著走進來，那筆錢是要買她先生的藥。她抱住我，還送我一張她兒子餐廳的免費晚餐券。那天晚上，爸媽說他們非常以我為榮。那種感覺比任何新遊戲都還要棒。

passages.title: 收據拼貼畫
passages.text: My art teacher, Ms. Yu, gave us a strange homework. "Bring every {1} you get this week," she said. We were all confused. On Monday, we brought them to class. Some were from the {2}, some from bookstores, and some from night market stands. Ms. Yu asked us to make a picture with them. At first, I didn't know what to do. Then I looked at my receipts and {3} something. Most of my money went to bubble tea! So I made a giant cup of bubble tea out of the receipts. My friend Amy made a {4} store building from long receipts. Ms. Yu hung our pictures in the hallway. "Art can show us our life," she said, "and maybe help us save some {5}, too."

blanks.why: every receipt「每一張收據」，後面拿收據做拼貼畫。cough、knee、fever 都不能帶到學校。
from the supermarket「超市的」收據，和書店、夜市攤並列。throat、toe、spoon 都不是開收據的地方。
noticed something「注意到一件事」：錢大多花在珍奶上。fried、boiled、spelled 接 something 在這裡都不合理。
a department store building「百貨公司大樓」。lemon、bean、sock 都不能和 store building 組成這個意思。
save cash「省錢」：cash 指現金、錢。fever、knee、throat 都不能「省下來」。

passages.zh: 我的美術老師余老師出了一份奇怪的作業。「把你這個星期拿到的每一張收據都帶來。」她說。大家都一頭霧水。星期一，我們把收據帶到教室，有的是超市的，有的是書店的，還有夜市攤販的。余老師要我們用收據做一幅畫。一開始我不知道要做什麼，後來我看著我的收據，注意到一件事：我的錢大部分都花在珍珠奶茶上！於是我用收據拼了一杯超大的珍珠奶茶。我朋友 Amy 用長長的收據做了一棟百貨公司大樓。余老師把我們的作品掛在走廊上。「藝術可以讓我們看見自己的生活，」她說，「說不定也能幫我們省點錢。」

passages.title: 百貨公司前的聖誕樹
passages.text: Every December, the biggest {1} store in Taipei puts up a huge Christmas tree outside. It is fifteen meters tall and covered with thousands of lights. This year, my family went to see it on Christmas Eve. There were so many people that we could hardly {2}. Inside the store, there was a special event. If you showed a {3} for more than 3,000 dollars, you could get a free Christmas bear. Mom had just bought a coat, so she got one for my little sister. My sister was so {4} that she named the bear "Tree." On the way out, a man in a Santa hat gave us a {5} for hot chocolate. We drank it under the tree and watched the lights change colors.

blanks.why: department store「百貨公司」。fever、knee、cough 不能和 store 組成地點。
could hardly move「幾乎動不了」：人太多了。fry、boil、spell 都不能形容人擠得動彈不得。
show a receipt「出示收據」：消費滿三千元就能換熊。throat、toe、spoon 上面不會有消費金額。
so excited that…「興奮到…」。salty、sour、spicy 是味道，不能形容心情。
a coupon for hot chocolate「熱可可兌換券」。lemon、bean、sock 都不能兌換飲料。

passages.zh: 每年十二月，台北最大的百貨公司都會在外面立起一棵巨大的聖誕樹。它有十五公尺高，掛滿了好幾千顆燈。今年我們全家在平安夜去看，人多到我們幾乎動彈不得。百貨公司裡有一個特別活動：只要出示消費超過三千元的收據，就能免費換一隻聖誕熊。媽媽剛好買了一件大衣，就幫我妹妹換了一隻。妹妹興奮得把熊取名叫「樹」。離開時，一位戴聖誕帽的先生給了我們一張熱可可兌換券。我們在樹下喝著熱可可，看著燈光變換顏色。

passages.title: 外婆的錢包與手機
passages.text: My grandma is seventy-five, and she still pays for everything in {1}. Last month, my cousin taught her how to pay with her phone. "It's easy, Grandma. Just show this code," she said. The next day, Grandma tried it at the {2}. But she pressed the wrong button and opened her photo album instead. The cashier saw fifty pictures of her cat. The people in line started to {3}, and Grandma laughed too. In the end, she took out her old wallet and paid the usual way. She also used a paper {4} for rice. When she got home, she showed me the {5} and said, "See? Paper never makes mistakes." But she still practices with her phone every night.

blanks.why: pay in cash「付現金」。cough、toe、knee 都不能接在 pay in 後面。
at the supermarket「在超市」結帳。fever、throat、spoon 都不是地點。
start to laugh「開始笑」，後面說阿嬤也笑了。fry、boil、spell 都不能表示排隊的人的反應。
a paper coupon for rice「一張紙本的米折價券」。lemon、bean、sock 都不能用來打折。
showed me the receipt「給我看收據」：紙本不會出錯。fever、knee、throat 都不能「給人看」來證明付款。

passages.zh: 我外婆七十五歲了，買什麼都還是付現金。上個月，我表姊教她用手機付款。「很簡單啦，外婆，只要出示這個條碼就好。」她說。隔天，外婆在超市試著用，結果按錯按鈕，打開了她的相簿。收銀員看到了五十張她的貓的照片。排隊的人都笑了起來，外婆自己也笑了。最後，她拿出舊錢包，用老方法付了錢，還用了一張紙本的米折價券。回到家，她拿收據給我看，說：「你看，紙從來不會出錯。」不過她每天晚上還是會拿手機出來練習。

passages.title: 用折價券交到的朋友
passages.text: Mrs. Chang, our new neighbor, moved in last spring. She was quiet, and nobody really knew her. One day, I saw her at the {1} with a pile of coupons. She was sorting them on a bench. I had a {2} for cat food in my pocket, but we didn't have a cat. "Do you need this?" I asked. Her eyes lit up. "My cat, Mochi, loves this brand!" From then on, we {3} coupons every week. She gave me ones for snacks, and I gave her ones for pet food. Soon, she was inviting me in for tea. Now she isn't {4} anymore, and I have a new friend. Last week, she even saved her {5} from the pet shop to show me how much money our trading saved her.

blanks.why: at the supermarket「在超市」。cough、knee、toe 都不是地點。
a coupon for cat food「貓飼料折價券」。fever、throat、spoon 都不能接 for cat food 表示優惠。
shared coupons「分享（互換）折價券」，後面說你給我零食的、我給你寵物食品的。fried、boiled、spelled 接 coupons 都不通。
not lonely anymore「不再寂寞」，前面說她很安靜、沒人認識她。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能形容心情。
her receipt「她的收據」可以看出省了多少錢。lemon、bean、sock 上面沒有金額。

passages.zh: 我們的新鄰居張太太去年春天搬來。她很安靜，大家其實都不太認識她。有一天，我在超市看到她拿著一大疊折價券，坐在長椅上整理。我口袋裡剛好有一張貓飼料折價券，但我們家沒有養貓。「你需要這個嗎？」我問。她眼睛一亮：「我的貓麻糬最愛這個牌子了！」從那之後，我們每個星期都會交換折價券。她給我零食的，我給她寵物食品的。很快地，她就開始邀我進去喝茶了。現在她不再寂寞，我也多了一個新朋友。上星期，她甚至把寵物店的收據留下來，給我看我們的交換幫她省了多少錢。

passages.title: 超市裡的捉迷藏
passages.text: When I was seven, I played hide-and-seek with my cousin in a big {1}. It was a terrible idea. I hid behind a huge pile of watermelons, and my cousin couldn't {2} me. Ten minutes passed, then twenty. My mom started to look for me too. She was so {3} that she asked the manager for help. Soon, a voice came from the speakers: "Will a girl named Lily please come to the front desk?" I knew I was in trouble. I walked out slowly. Mom hugged me first, and then she gave me a long talk. To say sorry, I gave her my birthday {4} from Grandpa to pay for the groceries. She kept the {5} and wrote on it: "Never play hide-and-seek in a store again."

blanks.why: a big supermarket「一間大超市」。throat、fever、cough 都不是地點。
couldn't find me「找不到我」。fry、boil、spell 接 me 都不合理。
so worried that…「擔心到…」：找不到孩子，所以請店長幫忙。salty、sour、spicy 都不能形容心情。
birthday cash「生日收到的現金」，拿來付買菜的錢。knee、toe、spoon 都不能拿來付錢。
kept the receipt and wrote on it「留下收據並在上面寫字」。lemon、bean、sock 都不適合拿來寫字當警告。

passages.zh: 我七歲的時候，和表妹在一間大超市裡玩捉迷藏，那真是個糟糕的主意。我躲在一大堆西瓜後面，表妹一直找不到我。十分鐘過去了，接著二十分鐘。媽媽也開始找我，她擔心到去請店長幫忙。很快地，擴音器傳來一個聲音：「請一位叫 Lily 的小妹妹到服務台。」我知道我麻煩大了，只好慢慢走出來。媽媽先抱住我，然後好好地訓了我一頓。為了道歉，我把阿公給我的生日現金拿出來付買菜的錢。媽媽留下那張收據，在上面寫著：「再也不准在店裡玩捉迷藏。」

passages.title: 回到 1990 年的超市
passages.text: Jake found an old watch in his grandpa's drawer. When he turned it, everything around him began to shake. Suddenly, he was standing in front of a {1} he had never seen. The cars looked old, and people were wearing big jackets. A newspaper said "1990." Jake was hungry, so he went inside. A bottle of milk cost only 35 dollars! He tried to pay with his phone, but the cashier looked confused. "Do you have {2}?" she asked. Jake checked his pocket and found a 50-dollar coin. "This coin is from 2015," the cashier said. "Is it a toy?" Jake {3} out of the store and turned the watch again. He was back in his grandpa's room. The only thing he brought back was a tiny paper {4} with a handwritten "Thank you, come again!" at the bottom. He never {5} it to anyone, but he still keeps it in his wallet.

blanks.why: in front of a supermarket「在一家超市前面」，後面他走進去買牛奶。cough、knee、toe 都不是建築物。
Do you have cash?「你有現金嗎？」1990 年不能用手機付款。toe（腳趾）、throat（喉嚨）、belt（皮帶）都不是付款方式。
ran out of the store「跑出店外」。fried、boiled、spelled 接 out of the store 都不通。
a paper receipt「紙本收據」，上面寫著「謝謝光臨」。bean、sock、spoon 上面不會手寫字。
show + 物 + to + 人「把某物給某人看」：他從沒給任何人看過。fried、boiled、spelled 都不能用「物 to 人」的句型。

passages.zh: Jake 在阿公的抽屜裡找到一支舊手錶。他一轉動手錶，周圍的一切就開始搖晃。突然，他站在一間從沒見過的超市前面。路上的車子看起來很舊，大家都穿著大外套，報紙上寫著「1990」。Jake 肚子餓了，就走了進去。一瓶牛奶竟然只要 35 元！他想用手機付錢，但收銀員一臉困惑：「你有現金嗎？」她問。Jake 摸了摸口袋，找到一枚五十元硬幣。「這枚硬幣是 2015 年的，」收銀員說，「是玩具嗎？」Jake 跑出店外，又轉了一次手錶，他回到了阿公的房間。他唯一帶回來的，是一張小小的紙本收據，最下面手寫著「謝謝光臨，歡迎再來！」他從來沒有給任何人看過，但他到現在還把那張收據放在錢包裡。

passages.title: 比圍巾還長的收據
passages.text: My friend Owen bought only one bottle of water at a convenience store, but the clerk handed him a {1} that was almost one meter long! Owen held it up and laughed. "Is this a receipt or a scarf?" he asked. Most of it was full of ads and {2}: 10% off coffee, buy one get one free on ice cream, and a free bag of chips at the {3} next door. Owen decided to use them all. That week, he saved 300 dollars. "This is the most {4} piece of paper I have ever had," he said. But his mom wasn't happy. "Think about how many trees we {5} on long receipts," she said. Now Owen uses the store app instead, and he still gets the coupons.

blanks.why: a receipt「收據」：買一瓶水拿到快一公尺長的收據。cough、knee、toe 都不是店員遞的紙。
ads and coupons「廣告和折價券」，後面列出各種優惠。fevers、throats、spoons 都不會印在收據上。
the supermarket next door「隔壁的超市」。lemon、bean、sock 都不是商店。
the most useful piece of paper「最有用的一張紙」：幫他省了三百元。salty、sour、spicy 都不能形容紙張。
waste trees「浪費樹木」：長收據很浪費紙。fry、boil、spell 接 trees 都不通。

passages.zh: 我朋友 Owen 在便利商店只買了一瓶水，店員卻遞給他一張快一公尺長的收據！Owen 把它舉起來笑著問：「這是收據還是圍巾？」上面大部分都是廣告和折價券：咖啡九折、冰淇淋買一送一，還有隔壁超市的一包免費洋芋片。Owen 決定全部都用掉，那個星期他省了三百元。「這是我拿過最有用的一張紙。」他說。但他媽媽不太高興。「想想看我們在長收據上浪費了多少樹。」她說。現在 Owen 改用商店的 app，一樣拿得到折價券。

passages.title: 在百貨公司走散了
passages.text: Last Sunday, my family went to a big {1} store to buy a gift for Grandma. My little brother Max, who is five, held my hand at first. But when I stopped to look at some sneakers, he {2}. I looked everywhere on the third floor. My heart was beating so fast. Mom told a clerk, and the clerk called the other floors. Five minutes later, we heard Max's name on the speaker. He was at the candy shop on the first floor! When we got there, Max was holding a lollipop. "A nice lady gave it to me," he said. Mom wanted to {3} for it, but the shop owner said no. So Mom bought a big box of chocolates there and paid in {4}. On the {5}, the owner wrote, "Hold his hand next time!"

blanks.why: department store「百貨公司」，有好幾層樓。fever、throat、cough 不能和 store 組成地點。
disappeared「不見了」：我停下來看鞋子，弟弟就不見了。fried、boiled、spelled 都不能表示人走失。
pay for it「付錢買它」：媽媽想付棒棒糖的錢。fry、boil、spell 都不能接 for it 表示付錢。
pay in cash「付現金」。knee、lemon、sock 不能放在 pay in 後面。
on the receipt「在收據上」寫字。toe、bean、spoon 都不適合寫字提醒。

passages.zh: 上星期天，我們全家去一家大百貨公司買禮物送阿嬤。我五歲的弟弟 Max 一開始牽著我的手，但我停下來看球鞋時，他就不見了。我把三樓找了一遍，心跳得好快。媽媽告訴一位店員，店員打電話通知其他樓層。五分鐘後，我們聽到廣播叫 Max 的名字——他在一樓的糖果店！我們趕到時，Max 手裡拿著一支棒棒糖。「一位好心的阿姨給我的。」他說。媽媽想付棒棒糖的錢，但店老闆不肯收。於是媽媽在那裡買了一大盒巧克力，付了現金。老闆在收據上寫著：「下次要牽好他的手！」

passages.title: 美國超市的巨大推車
passages.text: This summer, I visited my uncle in Texas. On the first day, he took me to an American {1}. Everything was huge! The shopping carts were as big as a small car, and the milk came in giant bottles. There was even a whole aisle just for {2} kinds of cereal. I counted more than eighty boxes. My uncle had a stack of paper {3} from the newspaper, and he used almost all of them. At the end, the cashier asked, "Cash or card?" My uncle paid by card, but I paid for my own snacks in {4}. I wanted to use the dollars I {5} for the trip. It felt like a small adventure. When I got home to Taiwan, our neighborhood supermarket suddenly looked very small and cute.

blanks.why: an American supermarket「一家美國超市」。cough、knee、toe 都不是地點。
different kinds of cereal「不同種類的穀片」，後面說數到八十多盒。lazy（懶惰的）、rude（無禮的）、thirsty（口渴的）都是形容人的字，不能形容穀片的種類。
paper coupons from the newspaper「報紙上的紙本折價券」。fevers、throats、lemons 都不能從報紙剪下來使用。
pay in cash「付現金」，和 by card 對比。bean、sock、spoon 不能放在 pay in 後面。
the dollars I saved「我存下來的美元」。fried、boiled、spelled 接 dollars 都不通。

passages.zh: 今年夏天，我去德州找我叔叔。第一天，他帶我去一家美國超市。每樣東西都好大！購物推車跟一台小車子一樣大，牛奶也是超大瓶的。甚至有一整條走道只賣各種不同的早餐穀片，我數了一下，超過八十盒。叔叔有一疊從報紙剪下來的折價券，幾乎全部都用掉了。最後收銀員問：「現金還是刷卡？」叔叔刷卡，而我用現金付了自己的零食錢，我想用為這趟旅行存下來的美元。那感覺就像一場小小的冒險。回到台灣後，我們社區的超市突然看起來好小、好可愛。

passages.title: 現金與刷卡的辯論
passages.text: In English class, Mr. Lin gave us a debate topic: "Is cash better than cards?" Our class was divided into two teams. My team was on the {1} side. "With paper money, you can see how much you spend," I said. "Kids who use cards often spend too much." The other team had good points too. "Cards are safer. If you lose your wallet, you lose everything," said Amy. "And many {2} stores give extra points to card users." Then Ben from my team held up a long {3}. "My mom paid by card last week and didn't notice a mistake until she checked this," he said. Everyone {4}. In the end, Mr. Lin said both teams won. "The real answer," he said, "is to be careful with money, cash or card. And always use your {5}!"

blanks.why: the cash side「現金這一方」，後面我說紙鈔可以看到花了多少。cough、knee、toe 都不能當辯論的立場。
department stores「百貨公司」給刷卡的人額外點數。fever、throat、spoon 不能和 stores 組成地點。
a long receipt「一張長長的收據」，看了才發現錯誤。lemon、bean、sock 上面不會有帳目。
Everyone laughed.「大家都笑了。」fried、boiled、spelled 都不能表示聽到後的反應。
use your coupons「使用折價券」省錢。knees、fevers、throats 都不能「使用」來省錢。

passages.zh: 英文課時，林老師給我們一個辯論題目：「現金比卡片好嗎？」全班分成兩隊，我這隊站在現金這一方。「用紙鈔，你看得到自己花了多少錢，」我說，「用卡的小孩常常花太多。」另一隊也有很好的論點。「卡片比較安全，要是掉了錢包，你就什麼都沒了，」Amy 說，「而且很多百貨公司會給刷卡的人額外點數。」接著我們隊的 Ben 舉起一張長長的收據。「我媽上星期刷卡，直到看了這個才發現被算錯。」他說。大家都笑了。最後，林老師說兩隊都贏了。「真正的答案是，」他說，「不管現金還是刷卡，都要小心用錢。還有，一定要記得用折價券！」

passages.title: 守夜的超市貓
passages.text: Every night after closing time, the lights in the small {1} on Maple Street go off, but one worker stays. Her name is Pepper, and she is a black cat. Pepper's job is to {2} the mice away from the rice and bread. She walks between the shelves all night like a little guard. In the morning, the owner gives her a bowl of fish. Customers love Pepper. Some children come in just to see her, and they leave her small gifts. Last month, the owner made a special {3} with Pepper's picture on it: "Show this and get 10% off cat food." Many people used it. On every {4}, there is now a tiny paw print. The owner says Pepper is the best worker he has ever had, and she never asks for {5}.

blanks.why: the small supermarket「那家小超市」。fever、cough、knee 都不是地點。
keep … away from「讓…遠離」：貓的工作是不讓老鼠靠近米和麵包。fry、boil、spell 都不能和 away from 搭配。
a special coupon「特別的折價券」，出示可以打九折。toe、throat、bean 都不能印圖片打折。
on every receipt「每張收據上」都印了小腳印。sock、lemon、spoon 都不是結帳時印出來的東西。
ask for cash「要錢」：貓從來不要薪水。knee、fever、cough 都不能當作薪水。

passages.zh: 每天晚上打烊後，楓樹街上那家小超市的燈都會熄掉，但有一位員工會留下來。她叫 Pepper，是一隻黑貓。Pepper 的工作是不讓老鼠靠近米和麵包。她整晚在貨架之間走來走去，就像一個小守衛。早上，老闆會給她一碗魚。客人都很喜歡 Pepper，有些小孩專程來看她，還會留下小禮物給她。上個月，老闆做了一張印有 Pepper 照片的特別折價券：「出示此券，貓飼料打九折。」很多人都用了。現在每張收據上都印著一個小小的貓腳印。老闆說 Pepper 是他遇過最好的員工，而且她從來不要薪水。

passages.title: 超市廣播的生日歌
passages.text: For Mom's fortieth birthday, Dad and I planned a surprise. Mom goes to the same {1} every Saturday morning, and she knows all the workers there. So Dad talked to the manager, and the manager {2} to help. When Mom walked in, everything seemed normal. But when she got to the checkout, the music stopped. A voice on the speaker said, "Happy birthday, Mrs. Wu!" Then all the cashiers started singing. Mom's face turned red, and she started to cry. The manager gave her a bunch of flowers and a gift {3} for 1,000 dollars. Dad paid for the cake in {4} and hid the {5} so Mom wouldn't see the price. Mom says it was the best birthday she has ever had.

blanks.why: the same supermarket「同一家超市」。throat、toe、cough 都不是地點。
agree to + 原形動詞「答應做…」：店長答應幫忙。fried、boiled、spelled 都不能接 to help。
a gift coupon「禮券」：價值一千元。knee、fever、lemon 都不能和 gift 組成可以使用的禮券。
pay in cash「付現金」。bean、sock、spoon 不能放在 pay in 後面。
hid the receipt「把收據藏起來」，媽媽才看不到價錢。cough、toe、throat 都不會印出價錢。

passages.zh: 媽媽四十歲生日那天，爸爸和我策劃了一個驚喜。媽媽每個星期六早上都去同一家超市，認識那裡所有的員工。所以爸爸去跟店長談，店長也答應幫忙。媽媽走進來時，一切看起來都很正常。但當她走到結帳處，音樂突然停了，擴音器傳來一個聲音：「吳太太，生日快樂！」接著所有收銀員一起唱起歌來。媽媽的臉都紅了，還哭了出來。店長送她一束花和一張一千元的禮券。爸爸用現金付了蛋糕錢，還把收據藏起來，不讓媽媽看到價錢。媽媽說，那是她過過最棒的生日。

passages.title: 兩百元的晚餐挑戰
passages.text: Our home economics teacher gave us a challenge: make dinner for your family with only 200 dollars. I went to the {1} with two red bills in my hand. I couldn't use any cards, only {2}. First, I checked the flyer at the door and found a {3} for eggs. Then I walked around and compared prices. I bought six eggs, a bunch of green onions, two tomatoes, and a small bag of rice. The total was 186 dollars. I kept the {4} for my report. That night, I cooked tomato and egg fried rice. My dad ate two bowls and said it was {5}. I got an A on my report, but the best part was seeing my family enjoy the meal.

blanks.why: went to the supermarket「去超市」。fever、knee、throat 都不是地點。
only cash「只能用現金」，和 cards 對比。cough、toe、spoon 都不是付款方式。
a coupon for eggs「雞蛋折價券」，從傳單上找到。lemon、bean、sock 都不能用來打折。
kept the receipt for my report「留下收據寫報告」。throat、fever、knee 上面沒有花費明細。
delicious「好吃的」，爸爸吃了兩碗。lazy、rude、thirsty 都是形容人的字，不能形容炒飯。

passages.zh: 家政老師給我們一個挑戰：只用兩百元幫家人做一頓晚餐。我手裡拿著兩張紅色鈔票走進超市，不能用卡，只能付現金。首先，我看了門口的傳單，找到一張雞蛋折價券。接著我到處逛、比較價格，買了六顆蛋、一把蔥、兩顆番茄和一小包米，總共 186 元。我把收據留下來寫報告。那天晚上，我做了番茄蛋炒飯。爸爸吃了兩碗，說很好吃。我的報告拿了 A，但最棒的是看到家人吃得那麼開心。
